UnitStatement: OpenPipeStress is a proposed free and open-source software platform for global piping flexibility and stress analysis.

The product implements open, classical, and modern mechanical analysis methods while requiring the responsible engineer to supply all code-specific, edition-specific, material, allowable-stress, component, SIF, flexibility-factor, and proprietary design data.
Core product concept: open mechanics in the solver; user-owned code knowledge in private data and rule packs.

The software provides a modern GUI, a transparent 3D line-element analytical engine, a user-defined rule-pack system, private material/component libraries, auditable reports, and a verification and validation program.

The software will not distribute ASME code text, ASME tables, ASME formulas copied from standards, ASME material allowable tables, B31J data, B16/B36 dimensional tables, or commercial software examples.

The product supports workflows for piping systems governed by ASME B31-family and other codes, but will not represent itself as an official ASME product, ASME-certified tool, or substitute for a licensed code, responsible engineer, or project design basis.
Piping stress analysis is fundamentally a global flexibility and stress-recovery problem; the primary model is a pipe centerline represented by line elements.
Piping components are represented by elastic members, rigid members, local flexibility modifiers, stress-intensification factors, and other engineering corrections.
3D solid or shell finite element analysis is reserved for selected local details, special components, or cases where the standard global pipe stress model is insufficient.
The user-supplied reference M. W. Kellogg Company, Design of Piping Systems (1956), establishes much of the historical and theoretical basis for this model.
Kellogg Chapter 2 (scan page 31) frames design assumptions, stress evaluation, and design limits.
Kellogg Chapter 3 (page 53) addresses local components such as pipe bends, miters, branch connections, flanged connections, and equipment interfaces.
Kellogg Chapter 4 (page 90) presents simplified flexibility-analysis methods.

Kellogg Chapter 5 (page 115) presents the general analytical method for flexibility analysis, including simultaneous equations, curved members, multiple planes, restrained ends, branched systems, and intermediate restraints.

The product updates this lineage using modern numerical methods: sparse 3D frame finite elements, unit-aware data models, nonlinear support solving, deterministic regression tests, and auditable digital reporting.
Commercial piping stress programs are powerful but expensive, opaque, and often difficult to audit at the numerical-method level.

Existing open-source structural tools generally do not provide a dedicated piping stress workflow with piping-specific components, load cases, rule-pack logic, private code data management, stress-result review, and calculation-report discipline.
OpenPipeStress will provide a credible open analytical core, a piping-specific modeling workflow, and a GUI suitable for engineering use.

OpenPipeStress enforces a strict separation between open theory and copyrighted/proprietary code data, a validation-oriented development process, and private project libraries and rule packs for licensed engineers and companies.
Product vision: become the leading transparent, auditable, code-neutral, open-source platform for piping flexibility and stress analysis.

The product lets a qualified user model a piping system, define materials/components, apply loads/restraints, solve the global flexibility problem, recover forces/moments/displacements/stresses, and evaluate results against user-supplied design rules and allowables.
Vision emphasis - Engineering transparency: calculations, assumptions, input values, and rule checks must be visible and auditable.
Vision emphasis - Copyright-respecting architecture: code-specific values and protected data are entered by the user or imported from lawful private sources.

Vision emphasis - Modernized classical theory: the solver implements the best practical version of line-element piping analysis rather than replacing pipe stress analysis with routine 3D solids analysis.
Vision emphasis - Extensibility: the architecture supports multiple codes, company standards, component libraries, and analysis modules without embedding proprietary standards.
Vision emphasis - Validation: the software is built around testable mechanics, regression cases, and published validation packages.
Primary goal: provide a free and open-source piping stress analysis platform with a dedicated GUI.
Primary goal: implement a robust 3D centerline/beam-based global piping solver.
Primary goal: support straight pipe, bends, branches, reducers, valves, flanges, expansion joints, rigid elements, and common support/restraint types.
Primary goal: allow the user to define materials, component properties, code allowables, SIFs, flexibility factors, stress indices, and load combinations.
Primary goal: provide a private rule-pack mechanism for code-specific stress checks.
Primary goal: prevent silent use of missing code or component data.
Primary goal: generate auditable reports identifying all assumptions, sources, missing inputs, warnings, results, and rule-pack checksums.
Primary goal: maintain a rigorous verification and validation suite.
Primary goal: avoid distributing copyrighted or proprietary standards content.
Secondary goal: support open exchange formats for integration with CAD, BIM, CAE, and plant design tools.
Secondary goal: support educational and research use through non-code example models using invented or public-domain data.
Secondary goal: provide optional local-analysis handoff to external FEA tools for nozzles, trunnions, lugs, branch details, or special components.
Secondary goal: allow manufacturers to publish permissively licensed component data packages.
Secondary goal: allow owner-operators and EPCs to maintain private rule packs and libraries.
Non-goal: OpenPipeStress will not ship ASME B31.1, B31.3, B31J, B16, B36, or other proprietary standards text, tables, figures, examples, or copyrighted code content.
Non-goal: will not ship ASME material allowable-stress tables.
Non-goal: will not ship B31J stress-intensification-factor or flexibility-factor equations/tables copied from the standard.
Non-goal: will not ship B16/B36 component dimension tables unless the data is independently lawful for redistribution.
Non-goal: will not claim to be ASME-certified, ASME-approved, or endorsed by ASME.
Non-goal: will not replace the responsible engineer, licensed code edition, project design basis, owner specification, or engineering judgment.
Non-goal: will not provide automatic legal interpretation of piping codes.
Non-goal: will not treat global piping stress analysis as routine 3D solid finite element analysis.
Non-goal: will not certify fabrication, examination, inspection, testing, or construction compliance.
Non-goal: will not guarantee suitability for nuclear, aerospace, offshore, cryogenic, toxic, lethal-service, or high-consequence applications without additional qualified engineering review.

The open-source core performs mechanics: geometry, section properties, stiffness assembly, load application, thermal strain, displacement solving, force and moment recovery, stress recovery from fundamental mechanics, and load-case algebra.

The user provides code-specific data: allowable stresses, code stress equations, code load combinations, code edition settings, material tables, SIFs, flexibility factors, component dimensions, manufacturer data, and owner-specific acceptance criteria.
Any missing code-required value must produce a visible warning or blocking error.
The solver may perform a mechanics-only solve with incomplete code-check data but must not report a code pass/fail status unless all required rule-pack inputs are present.
Every material, component, SIF, flexibility factor, load, allowable, and rule-pack value must support source/provenance fields.

Example provenance source categories: user licensed code, owner specification, manufacturer catalog, vendor calculation, test report, engineering calculation, public-domain source, invented example value, and unknown/unverified.
The primary analysis model is a 3D line-element representation of the piping centerline; local shell or solid analysis is an optional specialized workflow, not the default analysis basis.
The software must make it easier for an engineer to understand and defend a calculation and must not hide input assumptions, substitutions, or code-relevant decisions.
All input, internal calculation, output, rule evaluation, and import/export operations must be unit-aware; unit conversions must be deterministic and reportable.
Piping Stress Engineer persona needs to create flexibility models, apply project data, solve load cases, review stresses and reactions, and issue calculation reports.

Piping Stress Engineer key needs: fast model creation, familiar piping components, load-case and support workflows, reliable stress/reaction reports, manual entry of licensed code data, and an audit trail for all project inputs.
Owner-Operator Reviewer persona needs to review whether an EPC or vendor model is complete, traceable, and consistent with owner requirements.
Owner-Operator Reviewer key needs: clear assumptions, rule-pack identification, data provenance, missing-data warnings, and report reproducibility.
Engineering Company Administrator persona needs to maintain private company rule packs, component libraries, default project templates, and approved calculation-report formats.
Engineering Company Administrator key needs: private libraries, access control, versioned templates, rule-pack checksums, and no accidental redistribution of protected code data.
Open-Source Contributor persona needs to contribute solver improvements, GUI features, validation cases, documentation, and permissively licensed data.
Open-Source Contributor key needs: clear architecture, contribution policy, IP review gates, automated tests, and public validation cases.
Educator or Researcher persona needs transparent examples for teaching piping flexibility and stress analysis without relying on proprietary commercial software.
Educator or Researcher key needs: non-code example models, mechanics-based validation problems, clear theory documentation, and inspectable solver outputs.
User journey - Create/Analyze: create a new project, select a unit system, define design basis metadata, and create or import a private rule pack.
User journey - Create/Analyze: define materials with temperature-dependent properties, pipe sections, and component properties.
User journey - Create/Analyze: build the 3D piping centerline in the GUI and insert bends, branches, valves, flanges, reducers, expansion joints, and supports.
User journey - Create/Analyze: assign pressures, temperatures, weights, contents, insulation, and imposed displacements, then define primitive load cases and combination cases.
User journey - Create/Analyze: solve the model and review displacements, rotations, forces, moments, support reactions, and stresses.
User journey - Create/Analyze: run private rule-pack checks, resolve warnings and missing data, and generate an auditable calculation report.
User journey - Build Rule Pack: open the rule-pack editor and select a blank schema or company template.
User journey - Build Rule Pack: define stress categories, load combinations, required variables, allowables, and expressions using licensed/proprietary sources, then mark the rule pack private.

User journey - Build Rule Pack: software validates unit consistency and required input mappings, generates a checksum and version identifier, and the rule pack becomes available for private project use only.
User journey - Import Component Data: import a private component library file; software checks schema, units, required fields, and provenance.
User journey - Import Component Data: software flags records with missing source or required dimensions; user assigns components to model elements.
User journey - Import Component Data: report records component library name, version, source notes, and checksum.
User journey - Educational example: open a public example model with invented material and allowable values and solve a simple U-loop or frame benchmark.
User journey - Educational example: compare displacement and force results with hand-calculation references; no code-compliance claim is made.
The first MVP must establish the analysis foundation and data-separation model.
MVP must include 3D nodes with six degrees of freedom, straight pipe/beam elements, rigid elements, and linear anchors and restraints.
MVP must include weight loads, thermal loads, internal pressure metadata with basic pressure-derived stress recovery, and imposed displacements.
MVP must include a linear static solver, element force and moment recovery, and fundamental stress recovery.
MVP must include YAML/JSON project files, CSV/tabular results, and a basic GUI modeler.
MVP must include a rule-pack schema with placeholder/example non-code rules and blocking warnings for missing required rule-pack inputs.
MVP must include an initial validation suite and calculation report export.
Post-MVP: add bend elements with user-entered SIFs/flexibility factors and branch connection objects with user-entered local modifiers.
Post-MVP: add reducers, flanges, valves, expansion joints, and spring hangers.
Post-MVP: add nonlinear supports including gaps, one-way supports, lift-off, friction, and sliding restraints.
Post-MVP: add load-case algebra and range cases.
Post-MVP: add dynamic modules - modal, response spectrum, harmonic, and time-history support.
Post-MVP: add local FEA export workflows, an open validation manual, private library management, and CAD/BIM import/export.
FR-001 (Must): Create, open, save, and version projects; project file round-trips without loss of model, units, loads, rule-pack references, or provenance metadata.
FR-002 (Must): Support explicit unit systems and conversions; all numerical fields have units, incompatible units are rejected, and reports show units used.
FR-003 (Must): Provide 3D node and element modeling; user can create and edit nodes, straight pipe elements, and rigid elements in 3D.
FR-004 (Must): Support six degrees of freedom per structural node; solver supports translation and rotation in X/Y/Z at every active node.
FR-005 (Must): Provide pipe section property calculations; area, moment of inertia, section modulus, and mass properties calculated from user-entered OD/wall/density data.
FR-006 (Must): Allow user-defined materials including density, elastic modulus, Poisson's ratio, thermal expansion data, and user-entered allowables where needed.
FR-007 (Must): Support basic load cases - weight, temperature, pressure metadata, concentrated loads, and imposed displacements can be defined and solved.
FR-008 (Must): Solve linear static global flexibility problems; solver passes benchmark tests for beams, frames, thermal cases, and imposed displacements.
FR-009 (Must): Recover element forces and moments; local and global force/moment results available at element ends.
FR-010 (Must): Recover fundamental stresses - axial, bending, torsional, and pressure-derived stress quantities displayed independently of code checks.
FR-011 (Must): Provide rule-pack schema; users define private stress checks, variables, expressions, allowables, and load-combination mappings.
FR-012 (Must): Block incomplete code checks; software refuses to report pass/fail when required rule-pack values are missing.
FR-013 (Must): Provide graphical 3D modeler; user can create/edit pipe geometry, supports, components, and load assignments visually.
FR-014 (Must): Provide model tree and property editor; every model entity selectable and editable through structured property panels.
FR-015 (Must): Provide results visualization - deformed shape, support reactions, stress tables, and governing ratios viewable in the GUI.
FR-016 (Must): Generate calculation reports including input summary, assumptions, rule-pack checksum, warnings, results, and provenance.
FR-017 (Should): Support bend objects accepting radius, angle, orientation, user-entered SIFs, and user-entered flexibility factors.
FR-018 (Should): Support branch connection objects accepting geometry and user-entered local modifiers for header/branch checks.
FR-019 (Should): Support valves/flanges/reducers represented as rigid or semi-rigid elements with user-entered dimensions, weights, and source notes.
FR-020 (Should): Support expansion joints accepting user-entered stiffnesses, effective pressure area, movement limits, and manufacturer provenance.
FR-021 (Should): Support nonlinear restraints; gaps, lift-off, one-way supports, and friction converge for validation cases.
FR-022 (Should): Support private material/component libraries that are not redistributed with the open-source package.
FR-023 (Could): Support import/export; project and result data exchangeable using open formats.
FR-024 (Could): Support dynamic analysis modules; modal and response-spectrum modules pass validation benchmarks.
FR-025 (Could): Support local FEA export; selected local geometry and loads exportable for external shell/solid analysis.
The solver shall use a 3D line-element model of the piping centerline; each structural node shall support six degrees of freedom (Ux, Uy, Uz, Rx, Ry, Rz).
Each element shall assemble a local stiffness contribution into the global stiffness matrix.
The solver shall support local-to-global coordinate transformations, element-end force recovery, and result extraction in both local and global coordinate systems.
The initial solver shall implement linear elastic, small-displacement, static 3D frame analysis; later versions may add geometric nonlinearity and advanced material behavior as optional modules.
Minimum solver capabilities: sparse global stiffness matrix assembly, boundary condition enforcement, imposed displacement handling, and thermal initial strain handling.
Minimum solver capabilities: distributed and concentrated load handling, rigid-link/rigid-element support, and deterministic solution results.
Minimum solver capabilities: singularity and ill-conditioning detection and unit-aware result storage.
The straight pipe element shall support axial stiffness, bending stiffness about two local transverse axes, and torsional stiffness.
The straight pipe element shall support user-entered or calculated section properties, distributed weight, thermal strain, and pressure metadata.
The straight pipe element shall provide stress recovery stations at element ends and optional intermediate points.
The bend object shall support bend radius, bend angle, and bend plane orientation.
The bend object shall support user-entered in-plane SIF, out-of-plane SIF, and torsional SIF where applicable.
The bend object shall support user-entered in-plane and out-of-plane flexibility factors.
The bend object shall support user-entered pressure-stiffening or pressure-modifier settings where applicable and optional segmented visualization.
The software shall not supply protected B31J or code-derived bend values in the public distribution.
Branch connection objects shall support header element association, branch element association, intersection node, branch angle, and header/branch section assignments.
Branch connection objects shall support reinforcement metadata, user-entered header-side SIFs, and user-entered branch-side SIFs.
Branch connection objects shall support user-entered local flexibility modifiers and user-entered source/provenance for each local modifier.
Rigid components shall support length, weight, center of gravity, rotational inertia metadata, local orientation, optional semi-rigid stiffness values, and source/provenance.
Applicable rigid components include valves, flanges, strainers, instruments, specialty items, and equipment connection stubs.

Reducers shall support concentric/eccentric geometry, upstream/downstream section assignments, length, weight, offset vector for eccentric reducers, and user-entered local stress modifiers where needed.
Expansion joints shall support axial, lateral, angular, and torsional stiffness.
Expansion joints shall support effective pressure area, pressure thrust, and movement limits.
Expansion joints shall support tie rod/hinge/gimbal/limit rod configuration metadata and manufacturer data provenance.
Supported support/restraint types: anchor, guide, line stop, vertical support, directional restraint, translational spring, and rotational spring.
Supported support/restraint types: constant-effort support, variable spring hanger, rigid strut, gap support, one-way support, friction support, and sliding support.
MVP may include only anchors and linear restraints; nonlinear supports should be implemented after the linear solver is validated.
Primitive load types include dead weight of pipe, contents weight, insulation/refractory/lining weight, and component weight.
Primitive load types include internal pressure metadata, temperature change or total thermal expansion data, concentrated force, and concentrated moment.
Primitive load types include imposed displacement, imposed rotation, wind load, seismic static-equivalent load, hydrotest load, and user-defined occasional load.
Load-case distinction - Primitive analysis cases: directly solved load cases such as weight, pressure, temperature, imposed displacement, wind, seismic, hydrotest, and user-defined loads.
Load-case distinction - Combination cases: algebraic combinations or differences of solved cases.
Load-case distinction - Rule-check cases: user-defined mapping of combinations to stress categories and allowable limits.
The public software shall include a generic load-case builder but shall not ship protected code-specific load-combination requirements.
The solver shall recover fundamental mechanics quantities before code evaluation: axial force, shear forces, torsional moment, local bending moments, and resultant bending moment.
The solver shall recover axial stress, bending stress, and torsional shear stress.
The solver shall recover pressure hoop stress and pressure longitudinal stress if the user selects a pressure-stress method.
The solver shall optionally recover principal stress, von Mises equivalent stress, and Tresca equivalent stress.
Code-specific stress formulas shall be handled in user rule packs.
The engine shall use deterministic algorithms where practical, report solver residuals, and detect unconstrained rigid body modes.
The engine shall detect duplicate or near-duplicate nodes, zero-length or invalid elements, and inconsistent units.
The engine shall store input and output values with sufficient precision for engineering review and provide reproducible results for a given project file and solver version.
The rule-pack system is the key mechanism for code-neutral software, allowing users to define code- or company-specific checks without the public software distributing protected code content.
A rule pack shall define rule-pack name, version, code family or project standard (free text), code edition (free text), source/provenance statement, and redistribution status.
A rule pack shall define required material inputs, required component inputs, required project inputs, stress categories, and load-case mappings.
A rule pack shall define expressions, allowables, warnings, blocking conditions, and unit expectations.
The rule-pack expression evaluator shall be unit-aware, sandboxed, deterministic, and non-Turing-complete if practical.
The expression evaluator shall be free of arbitrary filesystem or network access and capable of basic algebra, conditionals, min/max, interpolation, and table lookup using user-provided tables.
Public rule-pack examples may include invented demonstration values but must not include protected ASME content or copied code formulas.
Private user rule packs may include licensed or proprietary information subject to legal rights and policies; the application shall mark such rule packs private by default.
The public repository may include rule-pack examples using placeholders rather than code-specific formulas.
Example rule-pack metadata fields: name, version, source, and redistribution_allowed.
Example rule pack declares required_inputs grouped into material, component, and project categories.
Example rule pack defines checks (e.g., sustained_example, displacement_example) referencing a combination, expression, allowable, and result_label.
Material records shall support material name, specification/grade (free text), density, and Poisson's ratio.
Material records shall support elastic modulus versus temperature and thermal expansion coefficient or total expansion strain versus temperature.
Material records shall support user-entered allowable stress, yield strength, and ultimate strength versus temperature where needed.
Material records shall support user-entered weld/joint/quality factors, corrosion allowance, mill tolerance, source/provenance per property family, and verification status.
The public repository shall not ship ASME material allowable tables.
Pipe section records shall support nominal size label (free text), outside diameter, wall thickness, and schedule/designation (free text).
Pipe section records shall support corrosion allowance, mill tolerance, lining/refractory/insulation metadata, and source/provenance.
The public repository shall not ship copyrighted B36 tables unless the data is lawful for redistribution.
Component records shall support component type, manufacturer, model, size/rating label, and end connection.
Component records shall support length or face-to-face dimension, weight, center of gravity, and stiffness behavior.
Component records shall support effective pressure area and movement limits (if applicable), source/provenance, and license or redistribution status.
Public bundled data: only invented, public-domain, independently generated, or permissively licensed data.
Private user data: user-entered standards data, owner data, vendor catalogs, material tables, rule packs, and component libraries.
Manufacturer-published data packs: permissively licensed component libraries supplied by vendors or contributors with documented redistribution rights.
The software shall flag imported data records when required fields are missing, units are missing or inconsistent, or source/provenance is missing.
The software shall flag imported data when redistribution status is unclear, data appears to be a protected standards table, or values are outside user-defined reasonableness checks.
The GUI shall include a 3D centerline viewport, model tree, property inspector, material library editor, and component library editor.
The GUI shall include a load-case manager, rule-pack manager, solver console, results browser, and report generator.
The 3D viewport shall display pipe centerlines, bend arcs, branch symbols, valves, flanges, reducers, and expansion joints.
The 3D viewport shall display anchors, guides, line stops, springs, and gaps.
The 3D viewport shall display node labels, element labels, load vectors, deformed shapes, reaction arrows, and stress-ratio color maps.
Selecting a model entity shall show editable properties: geometry, material, section, component attributes, and loads.
The property inspector shall show editable support settings, SIFs/flexibility factors, source/provenance, missing-data status, and rule-pack dependencies.
Missing-Data UX - Blocking for solve: missing data prevents numerical solution.
Missing-Data UX - Blocking for code check: mechanics solve can run, but code pass/fail cannot be reported.
Missing-Data UX - Warning: data exists but is incomplete, unverified, or unusual.
Missing-Data UX - Informational: assumption or note recorded for audit.
Example missing-data warning: cannot perform rule check because material allowable stress at operating temperature is missing.
Example missing-data warning: cannot perform bend stress check because out-of-plane SIF is required by the selected rule pack but not entered.
Example missing-data warning: mechanics solve allowed but valve V-101 has no source note for weight, so results are marked unverified.
The rule-pack editor shall provide required-input definition, variable browser, unit checking, expression editor, and load-combination mapping.
The rule-pack editor shall provide allowable definition, private/public status, source/provenance fields, validation diagnostics, and checksum generation.
The rule-pack editor shall not provide protected code equations as prefilled templates.

The component wizard shall help users enter valves, flanges, reducers, expansion joints, and specialty items, requesting required dimensions and properties without supplying protected standards tables.
Example valve wizard fields: component ID, valve type, end connection, size label, and pressure/rating label.
Example valve wizard fields: face-to-face or end-to-end length, weight, center of gravity, rigid or semi-rigid behavior, and source/provenance.
Calculation reports shall include project name, software version, solver version, git commit hash or release ID, date/time, units, and coordinate system.
Calculation reports shall include model summary, node table, element table, material table, component table, support/restraint table, load cases, and load combinations.
Calculation reports shall include rule-pack name/version/checksum, a statement that code-specific data was user supplied, source/provenance summary, missing-data warnings, and solver diagnostics.
Calculation reports shall include displacements, rotations, element forces, element moments, support reactions, equipment terminal loads, and fundamental stress results.
Calculation reports shall include rule-check results, governing locations, and a user signoff block.

Reports generated from public templates shall not reproduce protected ASME code text, tables, examples, or proprietary standards content; users may maintain private report templates at their own discretion and responsibility.
Reports shall include sufficient metadata to reproduce results from the same project file, solver version, and private rule/data libraries.
Verification shall prove the equations are implemented correctly; validation shall demonstrate the modeling approach produces credible engineering results within stated assumptions.

The validation suite shall include mechanics-based examples such as cantilever beam with tip force, cantilever beam with tip moment, fixed-fixed beam with thermal expansion, and simply supported pipe under uniform weight.
The validation suite shall include L-shaped thermal expansion frame, U-loop thermal expansion benchmark, torsion-only element, and rigid-link benchmark.
The validation suite shall include inclined-member coordinate transformation, imposed anchor displacement, linear spring support, gapped support, friction support, and branch assembly benchmarks.
Stress recovery tests shall include axial stress from axial force, bending stress from moment, torsional shear from torque, and pressure-derived hoop and longitudinal stress.
Stress recovery tests shall include stress range from two solved states, user-entered SIF multiplier behavior, and user-entered flexibility-factor behavior.
Every release shall run automated regression tests for unit conversion, matrix assembly, coordinate transformation, boundary conditions, and load application.

Every release shall run automated regression tests for thermal strain, force recovery, stress recovery, rule-pack evaluation, nonlinear support convergence (where applicable), and report reproducibility.

The project shall maintain a validation manual documenting test purpose, input model, hand calculation or independent reference, expected result, software result, tolerance, pass/fail status, and solver version.
Validation examples shall not be copied from protected standards or commercial software manuals unless written permission permits redistribution.
The public repository shall reject contributions containing ASME code text, ASME material allowable tables, ASME B31J tables or equations, and ASME B16/B36 dimensional tables copied from standards.

The public repository shall reject screenshots or scans of protected standards, commercial software examples or manuals without permission, vendor catalog data without redistribution permission, and any data contribution without provenance.

Contributors shall certify they did not copy the contribution from ASME, API, MSS, ISO, EN, CSA, ASTM, a commercial software manual, or any other copyrighted/proprietary source unless licensed for redistribution in the project.
Private rule packs and libraries shall be stored outside public example directories by default, marked private in metadata, and excluded from telemetry.

Private rule packs and libraries shall be excluded from public bug reports unless explicitly attached, and identified in reports by name/version/checksum without exposing protected content unless full reporting is requested.

User-facing disclaimer: the software performs piping flexibility and stress analysis using open mechanical methods, does not include ASME code text/tables/material allowables or proprietary code data, and code-specific values and rules must be supplied and verified by the responsible engineer.
User-facing disclaimer: the software is not affiliated with, endorsed by, certified by, or approved by ASME.
Before public release, legal counsel should review project name and branding, documentation language, disclaimers, and contributor license agreement or developer certificate of origin.
Before public release, legal counsel should review data-contribution policy, example libraries, and rule-pack examples.
The default application shall operate locally; no cloud service shall be required for modeling, solving, rule checking, or reporting.

Telemetry shall be disabled by default; if added it must be opt-in and must never transmit private rule packs, component libraries, material data, project files, or calculation results without explicit user action.
The product should support private library directories, redaction of private data from bug reports, and optional encrypted storage for private libraries.
The product should support checksums for rule packs and libraries and clear warnings before exporting private data.
Proposed repository architecture includes a core/ module containing geometry, units, materials, sections, elements, supports, loads, solver, nonlinear, stress, and results subpackages.

Proposed architecture includes a rules/ module (schema, evaluator, examples_non_code) and a gui/ module (viewport, model_tree, property_editor, load_cases, rule_pack_editor, results_viewer, report_viewer).

Proposed architecture includes data/ (schemas, empty_templates, public_domain_examples), reports/ (templates, audit, plots), validation/ (hand_calcs, benchmarks, regression_cases), and docs/ subpackages.
Candidate implementation approaches should be evaluated by numerical performance, sparse matrix support, cross-platform GUI support, maintainability, and strong typing and unit safety.
Candidate approaches should be evaluated by ability to expose scripting or plugin APIs safely, open-source dependency licenses, and ease of packaging for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Potential architectures include C++ or Rust core with Qt GUI, Python GUI with compiled numerical core, Rust core with webview/native GUI, and hybrid core library plus multiple front ends.
The core solver should expose an API supporting model creation, load-case definition, solve execution, and result extraction.
The core solver API should support rule-pack evaluation, report generation, and validation-test execution.
Performance target: solve small tutorial models interactively and solve medium models with hundreds of nodes in seconds on a standard engineering workstation.
Performance target: solve large models with thousands of nodes using sparse matrix methods and keep the GUI responsive during solve through background execution.
Performance target: provide progress, cancellation, and diagnostic logs for long solves.
Performance must not compromise auditability or unit safety.
The GUI should support keyboard navigation for major panels, clear icon labels and tooltips, high-contrast result visualization options, and search/filter in large model trees.

The GUI should support copy/export from result tables, undo/redo for modeling actions, project templates, inline validation messages, and clear separation between solve warnings and code-check warnings.
Release R0 (Architecture Prototype) deliverables: project data schema, unit system, minimal solver prototype, straight pipe/beam element, one or two verification cases, and command-line input/output.
Release R0 exit criteria: cantilever and fixed-fixed thermal benchmarks pass and the project schema round-trips.
Release R1 (Core Solver MVP) deliverables: 3D static frame solver, weight/thermal/imposed displacement loads, basic stress recovery, CSV results, and validation test suite.
Release R1 exit criteria: required benchmark suite passes within documented tolerances and the solver detects singular models.
Release R2 (GUI MVP) deliverables: 3D modeler, model tree, property editor, load case manager, results tables, deformed shape plot, and basic report generator.
Release R2 exit criteria: user can create, solve, and report a small piping model without editing raw files.

Release R3 (Rule-Pack and Private Libraries) deliverables: rule-pack schema, expression evaluator, private material libraries, private component libraries, missing-data blockers, and rule-check result tables.
Release R3 exit criteria: user can define a private non-code rule pack and run checks, and software blocks pass/fail when required inputs are missing.
Release R4 (Piping Components and Nonlinear Supports) deliverables: bend objects, branch objects, rigid valves/flanges/reducers, expansion joints, spring hangers, and gaps/lift-off/friction.
Release R4 exit criteria: nonlinear support validation cases converge and component provenance appears in reports.
Release R5 (Engineering Beta) deliverables: validation manual, full report package, IP contribution process, public issue templates, private-data redaction workflow, and signed releases.
Release R5 exit criteria: external engineers can reproduce validation examples and the public repository contains no known protected standards data.

Technical success metrics: number of verification benchmarks passed, regression-test coverage, maximum deviation from hand benchmarks, solver stability for large models, number of unresolved critical solver defects, and reproducibility of reports across platforms.

Product success metrics: time to create and solve a simple U-loop model, number of missing-data errors caught before report issue, number of usable private-library imports, user satisfaction from stress engineers, documentation completeness, and validation manual completeness.

Governance success metrics: number of data contributions with complete provenance, number of rejected IP-risk contributions, time to review contributions, and number of public examples verified as non-code/non-proprietary.
Risk: accidental inclusion of copyrighted standards content (High); mitigated by strict contribution policy, IP review, no populated code tables, and required provenance.
Risk: users mistake software for official code compliance (High); mitigated by clear disclaimers, blocking warnings, report language, and no ASME branding.
Risk: solver errors (High); mitigated by verification suite, validation manual, regression tests, and peer review.
Risk: unit conversion errors (High); mitigated by unit-aware data model and expression evaluator.
Risk: nonlinear support convergence failures (Medium/High); mitigated by active-set diagnostics, convergence criteria, user warnings, and validation cases.
Risk: missing component data (Medium/High); mitigated by blocking warnings and source/provenance requirements.
Risk: overreliance on generic defaults (High); mitigated by no silent defaults for code-relevant data.
Risk: GUI complexity delays release (Medium); mitigated by a CLI-first solver MVP, then GUI layers.
Risk: private data leakage in bug reports (High); mitigated by redaction tools and local-first design.
Risk: open-source liability concerns (Medium/High); mitigated by disclaimers, engineering review requirements, and legal review.

Allowable stress: a user-supplied stress limit or stress-value table used by a rule pack.
Bend flexibility factor: a user-supplied modifier representing increased flexibility of curved piping components relative to straight pipe behavior.
Code-neutral: the software provides mechanics and workflow without embedding proprietary or edition-specific code requirements.
Global piping analysis: a centerline/beam-style analysis of the piping system as a connected structural network.
Local analysis: a detailed shell or solid analysis of a component or attachment, usually performed outside the global piping model.
Primitive load case: a directly solved load case such as weight, temperature, pressure metadata, wind, seismic, or imposed displacement.
Rule pack: a user-defined set of required inputs, load combinations, stress expressions, allowables, and pass/fail checks.
SIF (stress intensification factor): a user-supplied local stress modifier applied during stress recovery or rule checking.
Source/provenance: metadata identifying where a value came from and whether it is verified, private, public, invented, licensed, or otherwise documented.
